title: Imagery: rehearse the stand
summary: How to run each target through in your head after the presentation: through your own eyes, at the speed of the real shot, once or twice per target.

body.html: Imagery, or mental rehearsal, means seeing and feeling a movement in your mind without doing it. Studies show it usually helps, especially alongside real practice, but nobody knows exactly how much.
The three points to run through in your head: pick-up point, hold point and break point.
body.heading: Watch the three points

body.html: Imagery seems to work better when it is close to the real thing: the same stand, the same targets, the real speed and your own point of view. The research is not from clay shooting, so most likely it works the same way in Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting.

html: Watch the presentation and decide the hold point, pick-up point and break point for each target.
Look at the ground or close your eyes and run each target through in your head once or twice, at the same speed as the real shot.
See it through your own eyes: the muzzles at the hold point, the target appearing, the gun coming onto its flight line, the break.
Rehearse a miss as well: see yourself breathe out, reset and break the next target.
Then step into your usual routine.

html.sporting: The targets are shown to the first shooter of the squad (Chapter 16 · Presentation of targets). Rehearse while the others shoot, not when you are on the stand and the clock is running.
html.compak: When Compak® Sporting is shot by squad, the first squad of the day sees the targets once, early in the morning (Chapter 17 · Squad: showing the targets). After a stop of more than 10 minutes, the singles are shown again. If your squad has six shooters, use the wait behind station 1 (Chapter 17 · Squad rotation through the stations) to run through the menu of your next station.

body.html: Rehearse in your head, not with the gun. Mounting and swinging the gun along a target's line is mock shooting: Sporting™ does not allow it on or off the layouts (Chapter 8 · Mock shooting and accidental shots). In Compak® Sporting you may not do it away from the shooting positions or while another member of your squad is shooting (Chapter 24 · No simulated shooting off the stand; no shooting animals). While targets are shown, the gun stays open and unloaded (Chapter 21 · Keep the gun open: turning round, target viewing, interruptions).
Some shooters hold their open, unloaded gun while they rehearse, so the picture feels real. Do this only where the ground and the rules allow it, and keep the muzzles in a safe direction.
In training weeks, you can try about ten minutes of imagery three to five times a week. Picture specific stands you know, and include the nerves you expect to feel on the day.
Imagery is not the same as hoping for a good result. It is a short, precise rehearsal of the shot you plan to make.

notes.html: Ask the shooter to describe one target aloud before the stand: hold point, pick-up point, break point. A clear description usually means a clear picture.

key_points.html: After the presentation, run each target through in your head once or twice, at the speed of the real shot.
See it through your own eyes: hold point, pick-up point and break point.
Rehearse the reset after a miss as well.
Compak® Sporting: if you wait behind station 1 (in a squad of six), run through your next station's menu there.
Rehearse in your head: mounting and swinging the gun is mock shooting.

did_you_know.html: Imagery can include feelings as well as pictures: the weight of the gun, the sound of the call, even slight nerves. Some shooters rehearse those nerves so that they feel familiar on the day.

quiz.q: How can you rehearse a target in your head?

options.text: In slow motion, as if filmed from behind
Through your own eyes, at real speed
Only the moment the target breaks

quiz.explain: Imagery seems to work better when it is close to the real shot: your own view and the real speed.

quiz.q: In a Compak® Sporting squad of six, when is a good moment for imagery?

options.text: Right after you call for the target
While the referee marks the score

quiz.explain: In a squad of six, the wait behind station 1 is time without pressure: run through the menu of your next station.

quiz.q: In Sporting™, why should you not mount and swing the gun along a target's line while you wait?

options.text: It tires your arms before the round
It shows other shooters your plan
It is mock shooting: not allowed

quiz.explain: Sporting™ does not allow mock shooting on or off the layouts; rehearse in your head instead.
